values.OtherEnglishNames: Yam Tethys Pipeline; Mari-B Pipeline; Tamar–Ashdod Pipeline; Tamar Export Pipeline; Yam Tethys Export Pipeline
values.ResearcherNotes: Physical asset is the pre-existing 30-inch Mari-B / Yam Tethys export line (transmission licence issued by Israel's Minister of Energy 29 Apr 2002; pipeline complete end 2003; Mari-B first gas Feb 2004). When the Tamar field came online in 2013, the Tamar platform was installed adjacent to the depleted Mari-B platform and hot-tapped into this same existing 30-inch export line to the Ashdod Onshore Terminal (AOT) rather than laying a new export pipe (Offshore Magazine 2013; Noble/ERM OPIC disclosure 2015 — 2 independent). Mari-B field depleted ~2013-2015 and its wells were plugged/abandoned in 2021; the Mari-B platform now serves as crew-lodging/storage for Chevron's Tamar operations, but the export PIPELINE remains in active service carrying Tamar-sourced gas. INGL's national map labels this corridor 'קו משדה תמר' (Tamar field line). ENDPOINT FLAG for the researcher: the INGL map appears to route/land the line near ASHKELON, but every engineering source plus the 2002 government licence give the onshore terminal as ASHDOD; 'Ashkelon' in sources is only the offshore field position ('24 km west of Ashkelon') and INGL separately operates a distinct Ashkelon reception station. Length ~42 km is single-lineage (Wood Mackenzie via hebrewenergy.com) and UNVERIFIED — not entered; route geometry DEFERRED pending a GIS-level source. Capacity ~6 bcm/y is the original Mari-B design (~600 MMcf/d), medium confidence. Current ownership percentages NOT cleanly re-confirmed post-consolidation (open item): original Yam Tethys partnership was Noble Energy 47.058% (op), Delek Drilling 25.5%, Avner Oil 23%, Delek Investments 4.441%; practical successors today are Chevron (via 2020 Noble acquisition) + NewMed Energy (ex-Delek/Avner) + residual Delek Group. Confidence overall: medium (existence/history/diameter/reuse-for-Tamar 2-4 sources; length/capacity single-lineage; ownership % and endpoint coords open).
values.Background: The Yam Tethys project (Mari-B, Noa and Pinnacles fields, ~20 km offshore Israel) was developed by a Noble Energy-led partnership under a 29 April 2002 Israeli transmission licence for a gas pipeline from the production platform to the Ashdod Onshore Terminal. Mari-B came onstream in February 2004 and supplied the Israel Electric Corporation. When the much larger Tamar field was developed, its platform was installed next to Mari-B in 2013 and tied into this existing 30-inch export line, which has since carried Tamar's gas to Ashdod.
values.FuelSource: Mari-B, Noa and Pinnacles fields (original); Tamar field (since 2013)
values.RouteNotes: Route geometry deferred: INGL map is schematic and the Ashdod-vs-Ashkelon landfall is unresolved; ~42 km length is single-lineage/unverified. Needs a GIS-level source before any route candidate is drawn.

values.OtherEnglishNames: Karish–Tanin FPSO export pipeline; Karish gas sales pipeline; Energean Power FPSO export pipeline; Karish–Tanin subsea gas pipeline; Karish gas pipeline (Dor)
values.ResearcherNotes: Subsea gas export line from the Energean Power FPSO (Karish/Tanin fields, ~90 km offshore northern Israel, water depth ~1,700 m) to a landfall at Dor, tying into the INGL national grid; matches the INGL map's 'קו FPSO כריש-תנין' (Karish-Tanin FPSO line). First gas 26 Oct 2022 (Times of Israel, Al Jazeera, Haaretz, Offshore Energy — multiple independent). Pipeline installed by Allseas, completed June 2020; shore tie-in at Dor completed by welding two 30-inch sections (Offshore Magazine). Dual-diameter line: 30-inch and 24-inch sections. FPSO nameplate gas-treatment capacity 8 bcm/y (~800 MMscfd); 2022 flow initially constrained to ~6.5 bcm/y until the Karish North tie-back (first gas ~2024) enabled full 8 bcm/y. Energean plc holds 100% (via Energean Israel Ltd) since acquiring Kerogen Capital's former 30% in late 2020/early 2021 — no current partner. OWNERSHIP NUANCE: per a 2019 Energean-INGL agreement, Energean transferred title of the nearshore ~10 km + onshore facilities INCLUDING the Dor receiving/OOAT station to INGL (~$102m); INGL owns/operates that segment, Energean the offshore majority — this is why the INGL map draws it as a supplier line into an INGL station. FLAG for the researcher: a gem.wiki page titled 'Karish and Tanin Fields Gas Sales Pipeline' appears to exist (surfaced in search, not opened per standing rule) — check whether a disconnected wiki profile already exists before treating this row as wholly new. Endpoint coordinates medium confidence (FPSO trackers disagree ~15 km; Dor landfall is locality-level) — RouteAccuracy capped at medium. Confidence: high on existence/status/start/length/diameter/capacity/owner; medium on endpoints and the exact INGL-handover completion date (open item).
values.Background: Gas from the Karish field (and later Karish North and Tanin) is produced and processed on the Energean Power FPSO, moored offshore northern Israel. Treated sales gas is exported via a ~90 km subsea pipeline to a landfall at Dor, where it enters Israel's national transmission grid. First gas was achieved on 26 October 2022. Energean took FID in March 2018 and, after buying out Kerogen Capital's 30% interest, holds 100% of the development.
values.RouteNotes: Candidate route staged (P8003.geojson, route-creation-tmng-map): traced from the INGL transmission map, ~87.5 km, capped medium (schematic source); it ends ~9.7 km short of the Dor landfall so the shore end needs GIS-level confirmation. Sourced length is 90.3 km (Allseas/Wikipedia/NS Energy).
